title: When AI Gets Cheaper, Do Prices Follow? Information Delays and Algorithmic Pricing
abstract: arXiv:2610.31693v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We examine whether lower costs of running AI models lead to lower prices, and whether delays in observing competitors' prices and limits on price changes affect how much consumers benefit. We study a simulated market with two differentiated sellers, logit demand, and tabular Q learning. A factorial experiment varies the age of rival price information, how often sellers can revise prices, whether production costs fall, and differences in firm quality and costs. We evaluate policies trained on 60 paired market seeds in each of 16 conditions, for 960 training runs, and measure expected consumer surplus after learning ends. translated_title: 当AI变得更便宜时，价格会随之下降吗？信息延迟与算法定价
translated_abstract: 我们研究运行AI模型的成本降低是否会带来更低的价格，以及观察竞争对手价格的延迟和价格调整频率的限制是否会影响消费者从中获益的程度。我们研究了一个由两个差异化卖家、logit需求模型和表格型Q学习构成的模拟市场。通过析因实验，我们改变了竞争对手价格信息的陈旧程度、卖家调整价格的频率、生产成本是否下降，以及企业质量与成本的差异。我们在16种实验条件下分别基于60个配对市场种子训练策略（共960次训练运行），并在学习结束后测量预期消费者剩余。在企业同质且成本下降的主要情境中，信息延迟与重新定价频率对消费者剩余的估计交互效应为-0.00025个标准化单位，其95%配对种子自助法置信区间为[-0.0402, 0.0393]。该区间包含零，关于相关检验的区间也同样包含零。（注：原摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本研究通过双寡头模拟市场中的Q学习定价实验发现，AI模型运行成本的下降并不必然传导为更低的市场价格，且竞争对手价格信息延迟与重新定价频率对消费者剩余的交互影响在统计上不显著。
en_tdlr: Using Q-learning pricing simulations in a duopoly market, this paper finds that falling AI model running costs do not necessarily translate into lower prices, and the interaction between rival price information delays and repricing frequency has no statistically significant effect on consumer surplus.
